## Owner's words

> my goal is seemless quick thought capturing ux

## Outcome

From anywhere in the App, the leader `⌘K` then one free letter (from `keys/chords.ts`) opens a one-line capture field. Typing then Enter files an Unassigned Todo in the active Project, and the field closes. Focus goes back where it was. Escape cancels with nothing filed.

- The capture costs two keys plus the text. The new row shows at once, and the Daemon confirms after.
- ⇧Enter files it and keeps the field open for the next one.
- A failed create keeps the typed text in the field, with the cause (U2773 rules).
- The key shows in `HELP_ROWS` and the hint line, from `CHORDS`.
- It adds no app-scope modifier key (U2241); it is a leader chord.

## Owner's words

> The user should be able to quickly add a todo with a quick shortcut and get into a mode of todo managment, nest it under the todos it depends on
> The user should be able to add todos and assign to a workstream or ask for a new workstream to own and be able to control when does that new workstream starts and how does it run concurrently in parralell
> The agent should be able to add and relate pads/section to the todos - a todo could have multiple refs pads/sections
> User should be able to leave comments
> The agent should leave comments(only when needed the user to read it) It must follow the hold:plain and use reduce etc.

The owner chose: one key chord from anywhere in roundup, with no ⌘K step.

## Outcome

⌘⇧T (or the closest free chord; the spec names it) opens the existing one-line Todo add field from any focused surface of an open Project, including a Terminal, with no ⌘K step. It keeps today's behaviour: ⏎ files and closes, ⇧⏎ files and stays, ⎋ closes, a refused create keeps the text and says why (U3713–U3716). The field shows the Owner and Home the new Todo will get, from the current selection.

## Scope

- One chord, listed with the other keyboard shortcuts; ⌘K then T keeps working.
- From a Terminal, the chord never reaches the Agent's input.
- Not an OS-wide shortcut.

## Regression

- U3713–U3716 capture tests; Terminal key routing tests.

direction.title: Quick add a Todo with one chord from anywhere in roundup

direction.body:
## Owner's words

> The user should be able to quickly add a todo with a quick shortcut and get into a mode of todo managment, nest it under the todos it depends on
> The user should be able to add todos and assign to a workstream or ask for a new workstream to own and be able to control when does that new workstream starts and how does it run concurrently in parralell
> The agent should be able to add and relate pads/section to the todos - a todo could have multiple refs pads/sections
> User should be able to leave comments
> The agent should leave comments(only when needed the user to read it) It must follow the hold:plain and use reduce etc.

## Outcome

A Todo holds a list of links to Pads or Pad sections. An Agent (through `rup`/MCP) or the user adds and removes them; the Todo shows them under its body, and opening one opens that Pad at that section. A link to a removed Pad or section shows as missing, never as a working link.

## Scope

- Reuse the `roundup://pad/<id>` link form and `link.read` (LK1, LK2), extended with a section anchor if the spec needs one.
- Several links per Todo; adding the same link twice keeps one.
- Contract change follows the Contract recipe (`.agents/builder.md`).

## Regression

- LK1, LK2; Todo create/update/history tests; Pad open tests.

direction.title: A Todo links to the Pads and Pad sections it relies on

direction.body:
## Owner's words

> The user should be able to quickly add a todo with a quick shortcut and get into a mode of todo managment, nest it under the todos it depends on
> The user should be able to add todos and assign to a workstream or ask for a new workstream to own and be able to control when does that new workstream starts and how does it run concurrently in parralell
> The agent should be able to add and relate pads/section to the todos - a todo could have multiple refs pads/sections
> User should be able to leave comments
> The agent should leave comments(only when needed the user to read it) It must follow the hold:plain and use reduce etc.

The owner chose: a queue with a per-Project cap; a Workstream counts as running while any of its Agents is working.

## Outcome

From a Todo's owner menu the user picks **New Workstream…**, which makes a Workstream that owns the Todo (its Home and its first Agent's work). The user picks when it starts: now, when a slot frees, or after another Todo is done. A Project setting caps how many Workstreams run at once. A Workstream counts as running while any of its Agents is `working`; one whose Agents are idle, ended or waiting on the user does not. A queued Workstream starts when the count drops below the cap, in queue order, and the queue is visible.

## Scope

- Starting a queued Workstream is the user's earlier choice spending usage (P9); a Daemon restart starts nothing on its own and keeps the queue.
- Changing the cap or the queue takes effect at the next count change; lowering it stops nothing that runs.
- Exact names (queue, cap, start choice) come from GLOSSARY.md or are added there.

## Regression

- Workstream create and Door start tests; Todo Home and owner tests; #3024 idle hand-off.

direction.title: New Workstream for a Todo, started now, when a slot frees or after another Todo

direction.body:
## Owner's words

> The user should be able to quickly add a todo with a quick shortcut and get into a mode of todo managment, nest it under the todos it depends on
> The user should be able to add todos and assign to a workstream or ask for a new workstream to own and be able to control when does that new workstream starts and how does it run concurrently in parralell
> The agent should be able to add and relate pads/section to the todos - a todo could have multiple refs pads/sections
> User should be able to leave comments
> The agent should leave comments(only when needed the user to read it) It must follow the hold:plain and use reduce etc.

The owner chose: a keyboard triage mode in the Shelf's Todos tab, not a board view.

## Outcome

The user enters a Todo triage mode from the Todos tab and handles every Todo with one key per action on the focused row, with no mouse: move focus (j/k), assign an owner (a), move its Home to a Workstream (w), nest and un-nest (Tab, ⇧Tab, as U3709), complete (x), comment (c, through the Todo comments Issue). ⎋ leaves the mode where it started. The mode shows its keys while it is on.

## Scope

- Reuses today's actions (`todo.assign`, `todo.move`, `todo.setBlockers`, `todo.complete`) and pickers; adds no new Todo state.
- Every action keeps U2773: a refused change keeps the user's input and shows its cause.
- Works on the final rows from #2900 and the owner groups from #3023.

## Regression

- U152 keyboard paths, U3708–U3711 nesting, U3723 row keys, owner-group drag tests.

vendorHelp.create:
Create an issue on GitHub.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video. The attachment is appended to the
body. If the body references an attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that
reference is rewritten to point at the uploaded asset instead.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.

If some attachments upload and others fail, the issue is still created with the
ones that succeeded. The command then exits with a non-zero status, but the new
issue's URL is still printed to stdout.

Adding an issue to projects requires authorization with the `project` scope.
To authorize, run `gh auth refresh -s project`.

The `--assignee` flag supports the following special values:
- `@me`: assign yourself
- `@copilot`: assign Copilot (not supported on GitHub Enterprise Server)


USAGE
  gh issue create [flags]

ALIASES
  gh issue new

FLAGS
  -a, --assignee login       Assign people by their login. Use "@me" to self-assign.
      --attach file          Attach an image or video file, in '<file>#<image alt text>' format
      --blocked-by numbers   Mark the new issue as blocked by these issue numbers or URLs
      --blocking numbers     Mark the new issue as blocking these issue numbers or URLs
  -b, --body string          Supply a body. Will prompt for one otherwise.
  -F, --body-file file       Read body text from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
  -e, --editor               Skip prompts and open the text editor to write the title and body in. The first line is the title and the remaining text is the body.
  -l, --label name           Add labels by name
  -m, --milestone name       Add the issue to a milestone by name
      --parent number        Add the new issue as a sub-issue of the specified parent number or URL
  -p, --project title        Add the issue to projects by title
      --recover string       Recover input from a failed run of create
  -T, --template name        Template name to use as starting body text
  -t, --title string         Supply a title. Will prompt for one otherwise.
      --type name            Set the issue type by name
  -w, --web                  Open the browser to create an issue

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  $ gh issue create --title "I found a bug" --body "Nothing works"
  $ gh issue create --attach './login.png#The login error state'
  $ gh issue create --attach ./before.png --attach ./after.png
  $ gh issue create --label "bug,help wanted"
  $ gh issue create --label bug --label "help wanted"
  $ gh issue create --assignee monalisa,hubot
  $ gh issue create --assignee "@me"
  $ gh issue create --assignee "@copilot"
  $ gh issue create --project "Roadmap"
  $ gh issue create --template "Bug Report"
  $ gh issue create --type Bug
  $ gh issue create --parent 100
  $ gh issue create --parent https://github.com/cli/go-gh/issues/42
  $ gh issue create --blocked-by 200,201 --blocking 300

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`
